title: Signs Before the Raid
author: Sergeant Osgar Redmane
pages: Raiders do not come from nowhere. They come from somewhere, and that somewhere leaves marks. Learn the marks and you will have a day's warning. A day is enough to bring the sheep in and bar the gate.
Smoke where no farm stands. Several thin columns at dusk means a camp of many fires. One thick column means a farm already burning, and the raiders already moving.
Crows in a crowd over the woods with no carcass beneath them. Dogs barking at the same tree line all night. Deer running out of the forest in daylight. Something walks there that is not hunting deer.
A pedlar who asks how many men keep the walls. Strangers buying arrows and bread but no cloth or salt. A shepherd missing two days. These are scouts, or the work of scouts.
If the Forsworn come, you will see crops trampled flat in straight lines and hear bellowing at night. Their beasts walk ahead of them. Do not go out to look. Ring the bell.
When the signs come, do three things. Send a rider to your lord. Bring stores and children behind the wall. Light every lantern at nightfall. Raiders prefer the dark and a sleeping town.
